column_treatments.description: Story 60.6. Joining N columns into one concept and splitting one column into N concepts, declared HERE because a mapping version is already immutable and content-hashed: publishing a change appends a version and rewrites no history (datastream-workbench-and-wizard.md:987). No table is added for them -- the only store that could have claimed one, app.datastream_derived_columns, is deprecated by the same story (AI-252) and carries zero rows. Optional: a mapping with no treatment omits the key, and an absent key is not an empty declaration.

joins.description: Each entry joins N named source columns into ONE concept. The source columns are NOT removed: they keep their row in the inventory carrying the word `Joined`, because hiding them is the same defect as hiding an excluded column under another name.

splits.description: Each entry splits ONE source column into N named concepts. One entry carries all N targets on purpose: N entries repeating the same pattern are two copies free to diverge, which is the defect story 59.5 repaired.

schema_splits.description: Story 70.1. Each entry splits ONE source column under a SET of positional layouts, the layout being chosen per ROW by a declared detector. Not in `required`: a mapping version written before 70.1 omits the key, and an absent key is not an empty declaration. One entry carries the whole set for the same reason `splits` carries all its targets -- three entries repeating one grammar are three copies free to diverge, and no column could say which of the three produced a value.

name.description: Names the schema set, and prefixes the three provenance columns it emits: `<name>_layout`, `<name>_token_count`, `<name>_token_count_matches_schema`. Those names are DERIVED and never declared -- a name that can be computed from the declaration is a second place for the declaration to be contradicted.

source.description: The source column read. Refused when this mapping does not carry it, when it is excluded, or when another treatment already claims it.

separator.description: What cuts the value into tokens. Never empty: an empty separator makes every value a single token, so no layout could ever apply.

remainder.description: The concept receiving what exceeds the last position of the chosen layout. Declared, never implicit: overflow silently truncated is a value that disappears without anybody being told. It becomes a quoted warehouse column, so it must be an identifier -- a name carrying a quote would break out of its quoting at read.

method.description: The MINIMUM offset at which an anchor token sits selects the layout. Declared as a word rather than implied, so a second method arrives as a second word and not as a silent change of meaning for rows already derived under the first.

anchor_tokens.description: The tokens the detector looks for. A token containing the separator is refused: a value carrying the separator is never ONE token, so it could never be found at an offset.

layouts.description: The positional layouts of the set. Two layouts naming one concept at two positions is the NORMAL case -- they are alternatives for the same row, never rivals -- but two layouts claiming one anchor offset is refused, because the minimum offset would designate both.

name.description: The value the `layout` column carries on every row that took this layout.

anchor_offset.description: The 0-based position an anchor token must sit at for this layout to be chosen. It must be one of this layout's own positions: an anchor outside the layout keys the detection on something the layout does not describe.

targets.description: The canonical concepts fed by positions 0, 1, 2 ... in order. The split runs from the LEFT; a row shorter than the layout leaves the missing positions empty and says so through `token_count_matches_schema`. Each becomes a quoted warehouse column, so it must be an identifier -- a name carrying a quote would break out of its quoting at read.

target.description: The concept the joined value feeds. Refused when a binding or another treatment already claims it.

sources.description: The source columns read, in the order they are joined.

separator.description: What is written between two joined values. An empty string is a legitimate separator (year+month+day -> 20260808) and is not the same declaration as a missing key.

pattern.description: One regular expression with named capture groups. Compiled at declaration time to refuse a bad one before a version is appended; never evaluated by the module that validates it.

group.description: A named capture group of `pattern`. A group the pattern does not capture is refused.

designates_object_kind.description: Story 68.2. The entity type (declared via 68.1) this column's values are keys OF. The binding lives HERE, in the mapping payload -- the governed, immutable, pinnable store -- never in a second store (governance.md:82). Optional and additive in the 1.x line: an absent key is 'nobody declared', an explicit null is 'declared: this column designates nothing', and the two are NOT the same fact (AC4). Same snake_case grammar as the kind itself.

event_role.description: Story 68.4. What this column CONTRIBUTES to a context event, when the file carries events rather than facts. A mapping declaring at least a `date` and a `label` role takes the events route: its rows land as datastream-owned context events (persist_context_event), never as facts. Optional and additive in the 1.x line; each role appears at most once, and a role is a DECLARATION -- the route is never inferred from the values.

template_id.description: A client-saved Template (fst_...) OR a catalog Template reference (template:<CODE>:<version>) -- the two ways file-source-ingestion.md binds one. Before AI-321 (2026-08-29) only the first spelling was accepted, so a human confirmation on a catalog-bound Datastream was refused by this schema after the gate had passed.

template_content_hash.description: The client artifact's sealed hash; EMPTY for a catalog Template, which has no client artifact to seal (its identity is the immutable (code, version) pair).
